“Turning Corners into Goals”

In the 2025 ISAC Sports Analytics Set-Piece Optimization Challenge you will dive into Liga MX HUDL Statsmobm 360 data and discover the tactical insights that separate winners from runners-up.

🎯 The Challenge

Turn five seasons of Liga MX corner kicks into simple, evidence-based recommendations a coach can use next match.

Visualizing sure is useful! But your submission should try and go beyond depicting trends:

  • Quantify effectiveness: Find if crowding the 6-yard box works better than spreading players out.

  • Model impact: What increases the chance of a goal — and the risk of conceding?

  • Recommend improvements: Replace 20% of outswingers with short corners—estimate change in shots & counters.

  • Communicate clearly: Use visual tools that staff can understand quickly.

Leverage StabsBomb’s OBV Power

Use On-Ball Value ™️ to uncover what truly drives impact in set pieces:

One of the biggest challenges in set-piece analysis is that most current approaches focus only on corners that lead to a shot — using metrics like expected goals (xG). But what about the corners that don’t result in a shot?

A key opportunity in this competition is to expand the analysis by examining all corners, not just the ones that end with an attempt on goal.

🎫 Entry Criteria

  • All participants must be Undergraduate or high school students
  • Teams can use any tools: Python, R, Tableau, Power BI, or even Excel. Use whatever tool you’re comfortable with.
  • International teams welcome — read rules for mentorship and prize eligibility.
  • Teams and participants must register through the form and provide proof of studentship.
  • Submit via the official google form before the deadline.

📫 Submissions

Your submission must include all three components below:

1. Final Deliverable

Submit one of the following:

  • Web application (with URL)
  • Research paper
  • Jupyter Notebook
  • Dashboard
  • Excel Sheet
  • Other creative format

Important: If using notebooks (Jupyter, R Markdown), export as HTML or PDF. Unrendered code files may not be considered.

2. Source Code

  • Complete, well-documented script in any language (Python, R, C#, Rust, Visual Basic, etc.).
  • Include clear comments explaining your approach.
  • If your code references external files, include all of them.

3. Video Demo

  • Maximum 5 minutes
  • Show your product in action
Language

Submissions strongly preferred in English, Spanish accepted.

Data Requirements

Use only the provided dataset and publicly available data sources. Submissions using private or paid datasets will be disqualified.

✏️ Judging Criteria

Category Weight What We’re Looking For How to Stand Out
💡 Innovation 15% - Are you exploring set pieces in a new or creative way? - Use unconventional features or logic
- Adapt tools from other domains
- Surprise the judges
📊 Accuracy & Methodology 20% - Are your conclusions supported by data?
- Is your process reproducible and sound?		 - Use solid statistical models
- Be transparent about uncertainty or assumptions
⚽ Tactical Relevance 25% - Are your insights useful to coaches or analysts?
- Could they realistically implement what you suggest?		 - Deliver specific tactical ideas
- Tie plays to squad types or situations
✍️ Clarity & Communication 10% - Can non-technical staff understand your message?
- Is the story clear and organized?		 - Write for clarity, not complexity
- Let your visual speak, not just numbers
📈 Visual Storytelling 10% - Do your maps, charts, or tools communicate? - Use pitch maps smartly
- Bonus for interactivity or animated setups
💻 KPIs 15% - Are you proposing a clear-well defined metric to evaluate? - We are looking for actionable insights
- Predictive & Stable metrics help

Good luck, and let your tactical imagination shine!🇲🇽

FAQs

What other APIs or libraries can be used in addition to those provided?

Participants can use any public data source to complement their analysis.

How do I access the competition data?

Upon registration, you will receive an email with the credentials to access the official competition data through HUDL’s API.

Should this focus on attack scenarios or protection scenarios?

You can choose either! The key is to first establish clear metrics or evaluation criteria for measuring performance. Once you have a way to assess effectiveness, you’re free to focus on whichever aspect—offensive or defensive—interests you most.

Is the competition entry free?

Competition entry is completely free. Submit through the submissions form before the deadline. Prizes are awarded at the discretion of ISAC and their judges.

Is this competition open internationally?

Yes, the competition is open to participants and students from all countries.

Can I work in teams?

Yes, you can work individually or in a team. There’s no limit on team size, but remember to list all team members in your submission. If nominated as a competition winner, the prize will be split between the team members, subject to terms and conditions.

How will the winners be notified?

Winners will be notified via the email address provided in their submission in late October. Make sure to check your spam folder and keep an eye out for communications from our team.

How do I submit my work?

You must fill in the submission form to enter the competition. Work not submitted via the form will not be considered in the competition.

Can I/ Should I share my work online?

We encourage participants to post their projects in public. If you want to promote your work on different platforms, use the hashtag #ISACHackathon
